acceptanceCriteria: A corpus build refusal for a bound or anchor violation names the offending path and line (and the bound), not only the error class.
corvint docs corpus build on Corvint's own docs scope at origin/main either succeeds under corvint-corpus-input/2, or the remaining refusals are recorded as intended exclusions with their paths.
Focused doccorpus tests cover the located refusal message.
body: Found while measuring V1-1982 (2026-10-19). At origin/main 547d26417cc9f559a77ab2fdc95721e1043a544c with Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 676: `corvint docs corpus manifest --scope docs` (rc 0) then `corvint docs corpus build --manifest <m>` refuses `corpus-refused: native paragraph bound exceeded` under corvint-corpus-input/1, and `corpus-refused: vacuous or oversized anchor` with the schema set to corvint-corpus-input/2. Neither error names a file or line, so the author cannot find the offending page in a scope of hundreds of docs. Corvint therefore cannot build a corpus of its own documentation (dogfood gap for the docs corpus/MCP server). Also: --manifest refuses an absolute path, which is surprising for a scratch manifest. Expected: a located refusal; actual: an unlocated one. Suspected defect for the self-build part (the content may genuinely exceed bounds); confirmed friction for the unlocated message.
title: docs corpus build refusals (paragraph bound, vacuous or oversized anchor) do not name the file, and Corvint's own docs scope cannot be built
